title: Adverb Position: 也, 都, 很, 太…了
description: Chinese adverbs sit after the subject and before the verb or adjective. Plus 也都, 不都 vs 都不, and why 很 is (almost) always there.

points.title: 也: also, too
points.summary: 也 (yě) goes **after the subject, before the verb** — never at the start or end of the sentence.
points.body:
- 我**也**是学生 (I'm a student too).
- 他**也**喜欢喝茶.
- With 都: **也都** (也 comes first).
- Not ~~也我~~ or ~~…学生也~~.

points.title: 都: all, both
points.summary: 都 (dōu) sums up the subject before it and goes **before the verb**. 都不 = none; 不都 = not all.
points.body:
- 他们**都**喜欢吃饺子 (They all like dumplings).
- 我们**都不**是老师 (None of us is a teacher).
- 我们**不都**是老师 (Not all of us are teachers).

points.title: Noun + 很 + adjective
points.summary: Adjectives don't take 是. A plain statement uses 很 (hěn), which here barely means 'very'.
points.body:
- 她**很**漂亮 (She's pretty).
- ~~她是漂亮~~ ✗
- Without 很 it sounds like a comparison: 今天冷 (today's cold — [unlike yesterday]).

points.title: 太 + adjective + 了: too …
points.summary: 太 (tài) + adj + 了 = too … (excessive), or exclaiming 'so …!'. The 了 belongs to the pattern.
points.body:
- 这个手机**太**贵**了** (This phone is too expensive).
- **太**好**了**! (Great!)
- Negative: 不太 + adj = not very (no 了): 不太好.

questions.prompt:
Where does **{也|yě}** go?
［A］{我|wǒ}［B］{喜欢|xǐhuan}［C］{喝|hē}［D］{茶|chá}。
questions.explanation: Subject + **也** + verb: 我也喜欢喝茶。
notes: 也 can't come before the subject.
也 must come before the verb 喜欢, not inside the verb phrase.
也 can't split 喝 and 茶.
也 goes before 是, not after.
也 can't end the sentence (that's English 'too').
也 can't start the sentence.

questions.prompt:
Where does **{也|yě}** go?
{我们|wǒmen}［A］{都|dōu}［B］{是|shì}［C］{中国人|Zhōngguórén}［D］。
notes: The order is 也都, not 都也.
也 must come before 是.
也 can't end the sentence.

questions.prompt:
Where does **{都|dōu}** go?
［A］{他们|tāmen}［B］{喜欢|xǐhuan}［C］{吃|chī}［D］{饺子|jiǎozi}。
notes: 都 refers back to the subject, so it comes after it.
都 must come before the verb 喜欢.
都 can't split 吃 and 饺子.
都 can't come before the subject.
都 goes before the verb 是.
都 can't end the sentence.

questions.prompt: Which sentence means 'None of them are students'?
questions.explanation: **都不** = none; 不都 = not all.
notes: Not grammatical.
不都 = 'not all' (some are, some aren't).
That's 'they are all students'.
很 goes before the adjective.
Adjectives don't take 是.
很 goes after the subject.
Adjectives don't take 是.
有 + adjective isn't grammatical.
在 = 'be at'.
吗 makes a question — the sentence ends with ！.
太…的 isn't the pattern.
很 goes before the adjective, never after it.

questions.prompt:
Where does **{太|tài}** go?
{这|zhè}{件|jiàn}{衣服|yīfu}［A］{大|dà}［B］{了|le}［C］，{我|wǒ}［D］{不能|bù néng}{穿|chuān}。
notes: 太 comes before the adjective, not after it.
太 can't come after 了.
太 doesn't fit before 不能 here.
questions.translation: This piece of clothing is too big, I can't wear it.
